newsitem.title: USA: US PLAINS FED CATTLE TRADE $64, OFF $1 - FEEDLOTS.
newsitem.headline: US PLAINS FED CATTLE TRADE $64, OFF $1 - FEEDLOTS.

text.p: U.S. Plains fed cattle sold at $64.00 per cwt in light trading, down $1.00 from Wednesday, but down $2.00 from last week's top, feedlot sources said.
About 5,000 head of steers and heifers that will likely grade select and choice sold in the Panhandle and an estimated 1,000 sold in Kansas, they said.
Fed cattle prices were pressured by sharp declines this week in beef values as packers discounted heavily to move product through the door, the sources said.
Losses were furthered by large showlists this week and projections for a large carryover into next week, they said.
Several feedlot sources said most owners were more willing to carry cattle supplies over than to sell at $64.00 because many would lose money at that level.
At $65.00, most owners were at breakeven or showing a slight profit, the sources said.
Weakness also was attributed to increased numbers of contract and formulated cattle supplies available to packers since August 1.
Week to date movement for the Panhandle was estimated at 75,000 head, including 30,900 formulated cattle to be shipped this week, USDA statistics showed.
Kansas weekly movement was estimated at 64,500 head, including 38,600 or about 60 percent previously contracted or formulated cattle, the statistics showed.
